key: What happened. Soldiers climbed the narrow path in a single line. Horns called from every side, but nobody could be seen. Guns fired from the bush. Then the hillside filled with people. The soldiers went back down the mountain.

key: The soldiers went back. This fight is fictional. It shows how a fight on the path may have gone. Soldiers really did attack Nanny Town in 1730, 1731 and 1732. In this war people were hurt and killed, on both sides. We do not show that.

key: What really happened in 1734?. Soldiers took Nanny Town in 1734. That is sure. A planter wrote, almost 60 years later, that many people were killed. One historian has argued that fewer than ten died. Another account says the town was already empty. We do not know what happened to every family. We do know the people built again.

key: The paper. Letters patent dated 5 August 1740 "granted unto Nanny a free Negroe and the people under command her & their heirs & Assigns for ever a parcell of land containing 500 acres in the parish of Portland." These are the real words, from a clerk’s short copy. The spelling is his.
text: The paper. Letters patent dated the fifth of August seventeen forty granted unto Nanny a free Negroe and the people under command her & their heirs & Assigns for ever a parcell of land containing five hundred acres in the parish of Portland. These are the real words, from a clerk's short copy. The spelling is his.

key: Today. Nanny is a National Hero of Jamaica. She is the only woman among the seven. Her people’s town is now called Moore Town. Maroons still live there. Nobody knows what she looked like. But her name is not forgotten.
